key_provisions_or_claims: Consumers should be informed when interacting with automated decision-making, be able to reach a human, and have decisions checked and corrected.
Calls on Commission to adapt product safety rules, including the Machinery Directive, Toy Safety and Radio Equipment Directives, for products with automated decision-making.
Urges a risk-based approach and a risk assessment scheme for AI and ADM.
Calls for review of the Product Liability Directive concepts of product, damage, defect and burden of proof.
Humans must remain ultimately responsible for and able to overrule decisions in professional services; algorithms must be explainable to market surveillance authorities.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 12 February 2020 on automated decision-making, consumer protection and free movement of goods and services. It urges the Commission to adapt product safety and liability rules (Machinery, Product Liability), adopt a risk-based approach, and ensure transparency, explainability and human oversight and review of automated decisions.
annotation.title_clean: Automated decision-making processes: Ensuring consumer protection, and free movement of goods and services
